summary: Seiren Matsunami (1903–1980) was a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji (~1927–1930) and under Walther Schubring (~1936–1938). He held professorships at Kyushu University (~1950–1967) and Rissho University (~1967–1974).

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology, Seishi Karashima (1957–2019) studied at the University of Tokyo, Cambridge, and Peking University, supervised by Xianlin Ji and Oskar von Hinüber. He served as professor and director at Soka University (~1998–2019).
Seishin Kato (1872–1956) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Toyo University. During his career, he held academic posts at Toyo University and at Taisho University (~1926–1943).
Seitatsu Matsunami is an Indology and Tibetology scholar. His career includes serving as a research assistant at the University of Tokyo and as a professor at Taisho University (attested 1992).
Seitetsu Moriyama is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. His career includes serving as a professor at Bukkyo University in 2002, with his affiliation there also attested in 2004 and 2013.

Seizan Yanagida (1922–2006) specialized in Buddhist studies and Sinology, studying at Hanazono University (~1939–1943). He held posts at Hanazono University as professor (~1964–1976) and director (~1985–1992), and served as professor at Kyoto University (attested 1986–1988).
Sen Wang (1912–1991) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University (~1931–1935) and later served as a professor at Minzu University of China (~1952–1991).

Senarat Wijayasundara works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. In 1999, he was attested as a teacher at the University of Kelaniya and as a visiting lecturer at the Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore.

Senchu Murano (b. 1908) worked in Buddhist studies, studying at Rissho University (~1929–1933) and the University of Washington (~1934–1938). He held a post as professor at Rissho University (attested 1972).

Sengaku Maeda (1931–2026) studied Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies at the University of Tokyo and University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown. He held faculty posts at Pennsylvania (~1964–1968), Tokyo (1973–1991), and Musashino University (~1991–2001).

Senkei Sakawa (b. 1937) is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his studies at Rissho University by 1965. He later served as a professor of Buddhist studies at Rissho University (attested 1981–1985).

Senmyo Naniwa (b. 1942) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned a PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University, studying under P. V. Bapat, among others. He was attested as a professor at Bukkyo University in 2005.
Sensho Hibi (b. 1932) specialized in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Rissho University (~1951–1959) and later held an appointment there as an assistant professor (attested 1972).
Sensho Kimura (b. 1943) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University (~1962–1971) and later served there as a professor (~1985–2013).

Sensho Murakami (1851–1929) studied at Toyo University and worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held teaching posts at the University of Tokyo (~1890–1901; 1917–1922) and Otani University (~1926–1928).

Seok-hyeong Kim (b. 1904) was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at Taisho University. He held academic posts as a professor at Dongguk University and as a part-time lecturer at Seoul National University.

Sergey Oldenburg (1863–1934) studied under Ivan Minayev at St. Petersburg University (~1881–1885). An Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, he was professor of Sanskrit at Saint Petersburg State University (attested 1897–1903) and served at the Russian Academy of Sciences (1904–1929).

Serinity Young (d. 2020) earned her PhD at Columbia University under Alex Wayman. A scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology, she held posts at Southern Methodist University and the American Museum of Natural History in 2000.

Seung-yeon Lee is a scholar in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology who completed doctoral studies under Sang-hae Lee. Lee has held posts at Sungkyunkwan University and the Gyeonggi Cultural Foundation.

Seunghak Koh studied Buddhist studies at Seoul National University and UCLA, completing a PhD under Robert E. Buswell Jr. in 2011. Koh served as an appointed researcher at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.
